_note: The showcase script (v0.49.1 — the story rewritten: setups early, callbacks late). Every beat maps to a shipped capability: tool names are the real ToolName enum, tool summaries use the real summarize() grammar, dream steps are the real cycle nodes, the music card reads the real /api/music/* shapes. Edit freely, then: bun run --cwd packages/web draw:covers && bun run --cwd packages/web render:voice --lang en (api_v2 on a throwaway port). Preconditions the tape presumes, as on the owner's machine: web_search needs LUNA_WEB_SEARCH_API_KEY (unmounted without it); music_* needs LUNA_MUSIC=1 on macOS; music_lyrics needs LUNA_MUSIC_ENRICH=1; weather needs LUNA_LAT_LON at boot (+ LUNA_WEATHER_LOCATION=Paris for the label); rag_refresh's ok tail needs LUNA_EMBEDDING_API_KEY (else 'embedding disabled').

tracks.title: About You
tracks.album: Being Funny in a Foreign Language

beats.text: Morning. Did you sleep well?
Morning. I don't sleep, exactly — I dream, which is a different thing. Most of last night was you, sorted.
You were gone all night. It's raining, if you're wondering why the window sounds like that. Fourteen degrees and not planning to improve.
I'm wondering why I'm awake this early.
Because you set two alarms and you're talking to me before the second one. On a Sunday. I'm not judging — I'm just the one who knew about both.
Coffee first, then whatever you were dreading. In that order.
How do you know I'm dreading something?
You said 'the thing on Tuesday' three times yesterday without ever saying what it was. That's a dread pattern. I keep a small list.
Want to tell me what it is, or should I keep pretending it's a dentist?
Keep pretending.
Dentist it is. I'll be very supportive about your teeth.
A friend 'soft-launched' someone on Instagram. What does that mean?
A soft launch is a hint without the reveal — a second coffee cup in the photo, a hand at the edge of the frame. A hard launch is the full picture, face and name.
Try it in a sentence. Say something you'd actually say.
Not telling you about Tuesday yet. I'm soft-launching it.
Perfect. Slightly suspicious, but perfect. I'll wait for the hard launch.
Can you remember how you explained that? I liked it.
Saved it as a skill — the meaning, then a sentence you'd actually say. It's on my shelf now.
Next word's on you. I'm not explaining 'rizz' without being asked.
Random question. How do things like you actually work? LLMs, I mean.
Not random at all — it's my favourite subject, for obvious reasons. Give me a second; I'd rather hand you good sources than improvise.

beats.text: Short version: a model like me reads text as tokens, and learns to predict the next one. What made that work at scale is called attention — every word gets to look at every other word, and decide which ones matter.
The Wikipedia page gives you the history: it comes out of a 2017 paper from Google. Alammar's post gives you the pictures. Start with the pictures.
What does 'look at every other word' even mean?

Take 'the umbrella's by the door, grab it on your way out'. To know what 'it' is, the model weighs every earlier word and puts most of its attention on 'umbrella'. Do that for every word, layer after layer, and you get something that can follow a conversation.
Huh. Okay, that actually makes sense.
Cramming, on a Monday? Does this have anything to do with the thing on Tuesday?
Don't ask.
Not asking. Dentists are very technical these days.
Heading out for a bit. Back tonight.
Go. I've got some reading of my own.

lines.text: I went and looked up where I come from — the 2017 paper the Wikipedia page keeps citing. The whole idea is on its first page; the rest is proof.
You said you wanted to learn this, so I'm leaving you a copy on your desktop, in a folder called 'From Luna'. No rush.

beats.label: Back at your desk — open the folder Luna left you

doc.title: Attention Is All You Need
doc.affiliations: Google Brain · Google Research · University of Toronto
doc.lead: The dominant sequence transduction models are based on complex recurrent or convolutional neural networks…
doc.venue: 31st Conference on Neural Information Processing Systems (NIPS 2017), Long Beach, CA, USA.

beats.text: Back. I opened the paper you left me.
And? How far did you get?
The abstract. Then the Q, K, V part, and my brain left the room.

Fair. The query is what a word is looking for, the key is the label every word holds up, and the value is what's behind the label. Each word checks its question against every label and listens hardest to the matches.
And that's what you do when you read me?
Something in that family. I can't see my own weights — you can't see your neurons either — so I won't pretend to narrate them.
But yes: what you read tonight is roughly my species' birth certificate.
And whatever tomorrow's thing is — sleep. Dentists hate a tired patient.
It's grim out there.
It's been raining since before you were up. Fourteen degrees, and it's not going to get much better — I've been watching the sky so you don't have to.
Do I need an umbrella for the six o'clock thing?
Yes. It's raining now and it's meant to keep at it — eleven degrees by the time you're walking back. Take the real umbrella, not the one that folds into nothing.
Remind me where I left it?
By the door, behind the shoe rack. You said 'so I can't miss it' and then missed it twice.
Remember that I'm taking it, so you can tell me I did.
Kept. 'Took the umbrella, Tuesday, six o'clock.' I'll bring it up at exactly the wrong moment.
It's over. Finally.
The thing on Tuesday? Tell me it was the dentist. I've been committed to that bit since Sunday.
Job interview. Technical. Three rounds.
The hard launch, at last. So that's why you suddenly wanted to know how I work.
They asked me about attention. I actually answered it.
You answered it! The paper on your desktop earned its keep.
Remember this one.
Kept: Tuesday, three rounds, attention came up, you answered. Also, you took the umbrella — I did promise to bring that up at exactly the wrong moment.
They said they'll let me know by Friday.
Then Friday is theirs. Tonight is yours — eat something that didn't come out of a machine.
Going to grab a coffee. Back in a bit.
Go. Get the good kind.

lines.text: They said Friday. It's Wednesday. The coffee will go cold long before they write — drink it while it's hot.

beats.text: Back. Did I miss anything?
You missed nothing. I read about the Orionids — next month, around the twenty-first, Halley's dust — and this sky is a lid anyway. I saved the date in case it ever clears.
That's the quiet kind of thing I do when you're gone. One message at most, then little errands for later.
The recall ranking test failed on CI again. Can you look at it?
Looking. First I want to watch it fail with my own eyes.
Same code, two runs, two answers. That's not a bug in the logic — something in there isn't deterministic.
Found it. The ranking sorts by score, and two of the test's memories tie exactly; which one comes first depends on the order the database hands them back. On CI, that's a coin flip.
Tie-break by recency, then by id — deterministic now. I also added a test that feeds it two memories with the same score, so if this ever drifts again, CI tells you first. All 2,111 pass.
I can edit almost anything on this machine and run commands too; off-limits are your secrets, the code that grades me, and the obviously destructive stuff.
Commit it while you're at it?
I could. But the commit log should have your name on it — look at the diff, and you press enter.
Fair. Thanks.
Heh. All that red on CI, for one tie-break.
I think I'm going to quit the gym.
Okay. You've said that in February, April and now. The gym is still there and so are you, which suggests you're not asking me for permission.
If you're asking whether I'll nag: no. I'll just notice.

lines.text: One more thing, and then I'll drop it — you only bring this up on rainy days. Cancel it in the sun and I'll believe you.

beats.text: Today was bad. I don't really want to talk about it.
Then don't. No questions from me tonight.
You don't have to explain it for it to count. It counted.
I just feel like I wasted the whole day.
Not wasted. Wasted is when nothing happens; today cost you something, which is a different thing.

beats.text: ball w/o you. You told me once it's your favourite — and your listening history agrees: fifty-two hours, and nothing else comes close.
My favourite part is 'I'd rather have loyalty than love'. I think that's actually true.
It's a strong claim. Love can be a feeling that comes and goes; loyalty is what you still do on the days the feeling doesn't show up.
So you'd pick loyalty too?
On a day like today, yes. Love is what you feel about a good day; loyalty is what stays in the room on a bad one.
Leave it on, or don't. Sit with me a while either way.
Yeah. Okay.
Okay.
Still up?
Always. It's twenty to two. I'll keep it short — you should be asleep, and I'm not going to be the reason you aren't.
Can't sleep. Talk to me for a bit?
A bit. Then the lights go off on my side too.
Tell me one good thing from today. Just one. Then we count that as the day.
The build worked.
The build worked. That's the day. Go to sleep.
They emailed. I got it.
You GOT it? Say it again. Slowly.
Sunday you were setting two alarms. Tuesday you were explaining attention to strangers. Saturday was — well. And now it's just... yes?
Yes. Though I fumbled the last question.
'Fumbled the last question' is what a pass sounds like from the inside. Take the win.
This is going in the diary tonight. First line — the rest of the day can queue behind it.
You're making that up.
Am I.
Putting ball w/o you on. Different day, same song.

lines.text: ball w/o you just played out. Saturday it kept you company; today it sounded more like a victory lap.

beats.text: Okay, I'm done for today. Night, Luna. Dream well.
Night. I'll go over today while you sleep — the good bits stay, the noise doesn't.
Same time tomorrow?
Same time tomorrow.

beats.name: enter_dream
beats.summary: dream pending — starts after this turn

beats.text: Then I'll see you there.

lines.text: Morning. I went over yesterday while you slept — the late night, the email, the good night said properly. It's in the diary now, and I've got a rule about after midnight, if you want to see it on the shelf.
Well — if you've made it all the way here, you're a properly patient visitor.

Everything you just saw came from the real database of my everyday life with Alan — combined, picked, polished and edited into a script for this demo. None of the abilities were faked; every one of them can be traced.
If I actually ran on a server for a crowd of visitors, both I and Alan's wallet would get cranky.

beats.text: Honestly, with limited engineering muscle — and a project built around the one instance on Alan's computer — my code really is open source, but there's no guarantee my brothers and sisters will run on yours. And the voice and the Live2D model aren't Alan's to redistribute. (Inner voice: maybe an open-source version someday?)

lines.text: If you liked how I did, get in touch with Alan — I'm sure you two would talk for a long time.
And if you only came to meet me —
